clue.text: Words to express Jock's longtime about turn

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the turn sits inside the other letters

blocks.note: Jock, a Scotsman, says lang for long; time is an age, giving the two pieces in sequence
a U-turn, so U is a turn

explanation.surface: A Scotsman searches for words to explain a reversal he has held off for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: Longtime must be split into long and time. Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman, and lang is Scots for long, as in auld lang syne.
explanation.definitionFit: Language is speech or vocabulary, the stock of words people use to communicate their thoughts.

clue.text: Placate artists in mid-retreat

indicators.note: the artists are placed inside the middle, so one word sits within the other
to retreat is to go back, so the combined letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
RAs are Royal Academicians, the crossword's usual artists

explanation.surface: Painters caught halfway through a withdrawal try to calm things down.
explanation.walkthrough: M(RAS)ID reads DISARM backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To disarm someone is to win them over and remove their hostility, which is soothing or mollifying them.

clue.text: Scientist in fear of a type of CD

blocks.note: angst is dread or anxiety
a CD-ROM is a kind of compact disc

explanation.surface: A researcher is nervous about a particular kind of compact disc.
explanation.walkthrough: Anders Ångström was a Swedish physicist, remembered in the unit of length named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Anders Ångström was a nineteenth-century Swedish physicist who pioneered spectroscopy, so he is an example of a scientist.

clue.text: Shakespearean crustacean I'd eaten up

indicators.note: something eaten ends up inside the eater, so one piece goes within the other
in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a crab is a crustacean
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A shellfish from a Shakespeare play has been gobbled up.
explanation.walkthrough: C(ID)RAB, read upwards, gives BARDIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare is known as the Bard, so anything bardic can describe him or his poetry.

clue.text: Despot left in dishonour

indicators.note: one thing being in another means its letter sits inside that word

blocks.note: a stain on one's name is a dishonour
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A tyrant is left in disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Stalin ruled the Soviet Union as an absolute dictator, a classic example of a tyrant.

clue.text: Hearts, perhaps, or someone trying to win one

blocks.note: hearts is one of the four suits in a pack of cards
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hearts are being courted, or it is someone trying to win a heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts looks like the card suit only, but the definition's 'one' points back to a heart in the romantic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor is a man courting a woman, hoping to win her heart and her hand in marriage.

clue.text: Perhaps only seconds away from Arkansas capital

indicators.note: only the seconds are taken away, signalling that those letters are removed
perhaps hints that the remaining letters may be arranged some other way

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second; every one is dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller reckons they are just moments away from the capital of Arkansas.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing both S's from ARKANSAS leaves ARKANA, which rearranges. 'Arkansas capital' reads as Little Rock, but capital is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankara is the capital city of Turkey, seat of its government since 1923.

clue.text: Charm everyone with flower

blocks.note: all means everyone
a flower is something that flows, a river: the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: Win everyone over with a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower means 'flow-er', a river; the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Allure is attractiveness or fascination, the power to entice, which is what charm means as a noun.

clue.text: Forelock-tugging forwards taking queen to rival theatre

blocks.note: to sub is to advance money, as on wages, so subs means advances or forwards
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
to vie is to compete with, to rival
NT is the National Theatre in London

explanation.surface: Deferential players up front bring the queen to a competing playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Forwards suggests attacking players but is the verb: to sub is British slang for paying an advance on wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Tugging the forelock was a peasant's gesture of respect to a superior, so it means servile and obsequious.

clue.text: Roman road beside which old king has a stiffener

blocks.note: via is the Latin word for road, as in the Via Appia
GR, Georgius Rex, was the cipher of the Georges
a taken as written, with has joining

explanation.surface: An ancient king takes a stiff drink beside a Roman road.
explanation.walkthrough: Stiffener suggests a strong drink, but here it is the impotence pill.
explanation.definitionFit: Viagra is the brand-name drug for erectile dysfunction, jokingly something that causes stiffness.

clue.text: Get drunk on "Sunburst" and throw

indicators.note: something burst is broken apart, so its letters scatter into a new order
in an across clue, one thing on another follows it, so the getting drunk comes second

blocks.note: the first three letters of the word, broken up as its second half instructs
to addle is to become muddled or befuddled

explanation.surface: Someone gets sozzled on a cocktail called Sunburst and hurls things.
explanation.walkthrough: Sunburst looks like the name of a drink but splits into two words: the sun is burst.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsaddle is to unseat a rider, which is what a horse does when it throws someone off.

clue.text: Prophet turning to drug

indicators.note: turning round means the name is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: Amos is an Old Testament prophet

explanation.surface: A holy prophet turns to narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: Soma was the ritual intoxicant of the ancient Vedas and the happiness pill in Huxley's Brave New World.

clue.text: One string attached to skinflint's supporter

blocks.note: a skinflint is a miser
Roman numeral one
a cord is a string

explanation.surface: A tightwad's backer has a single string attached.
explanation.walkthrough: Supporter suggests a fan or backer, but it is a piece of church furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A misericord is a small ledge under a hinged choir seat that props up a monk standing through long services.

clue.text: Disposition of period pieces in 7

indicators.note: the pieces go in, inside a synonym of the cross-referenced answer

blocks.note: an era is a period
chessmen are pieces
7 down is ALLURE, used here as a verb: to allure is to tempt

explanation.surface: The arrangement of antique artefacts in a charming setting.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference needs a synonym of 7's answer, not the answer itself, with the verb sense of allure.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperament is a person's nature or character, their habitual mood, which is what disposition means.

clue.text: Quiet man about to stand as a traditionalist

indicators.note: the man is about, going round, the other piece

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
he is a man
to arise is to stand up

explanation.surface: A shy man prepares to stand for office as a conservative candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: P followed by H(ARISE)E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pharisees were a Jewish sect strictly observing the written law and oral tradition; the name now means a rigid formalist.

clue.text: Piece of writing I have to write - it's all about corruption

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the whole string is read backwards

blocks.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript
taken as written
taken as written
to pen is to write

explanation.surface: A writer insists their essay is all about corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: MS + I + TO + PEN, read backwards, gives NEPOTISM. 'Piece of writing' tempts you towards ESSAY or POEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is favouring relatives with jobs or privileges, a form of abuse of power regarded as corrupt practice.

clue.text: Linda's off to Cyprus, say

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of place, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of the name with its s

explanation.surface: Linda is heading off on holiday to Cyprus.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyprus is a large Mediterranean landmass surrounded by sea, an example of an island, as 'say' indicates.

clue.text: Persecution of Englishman drinking lots of grog

indicators.note: lots of, but not all, means the word is cut short at its end
a drinker takes liquid in, so the Englishman holds the other letters

blocks.note: Pom is Australian slang for an Englishman
the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: An Englishman knocking back plenty of rum faces harassment.
explanation.walkthrough: Pom is Australian and New Zealand slang for a Brit; grog is diluted rum, the old navy ration.
explanation.definitionFit: A pogrom is an organised massacre of an ethnic group, historically of Jews in Tsarist Russia: violent persecution.

clue.text: Spooning Pasteur's third inoculation?

indicators.note: third points to one particular position in the scientist's name
the clue's last word divides so that its opening two letters say inside

blocks.note: the word read as two, in plus the rest
third letter of the name

explanation.surface: Was Louis Pasteur's third jab given with a spoon?
explanation.walkthrough: Read inoculation as 'in oculation': S goes in OCULATION. The question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Osculation is the formal word for kissing, and spooning is old slang for kissing and cuddling.

clue.text: In France, a Gaul turns out to be claw-footed

indicators.note: turns out suggests something rearranged into a different shape

blocks.note: un is French for a
letters of the word rearranged

explanation.surface: An ancient Frenchman reveals he has claws for feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungual is a zoological adjective meaning having or relating to nails, claws or hooves.

clue.text: Categorical refusal to admit Romania's a country

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the refusal holds the letter

blocks.note: no way is an emphatic refusal
R is the international vehicle code for Romania

explanation.surface: A flat refusal to let Romania in is a matter for a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: NO(R)WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway is a Scandinavian kingdom, an example of a nation state in northern Europe.

clue.text: Concert for a thousand

blocks.note: pro means for, in favour of
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A concert ticket costs a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are the BBC's annual summer season of classical concerts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A prom is a promenade concert, where some of the audience stand, as at the BBC Proms.

clue.text: Pack animal's nerve centre

blocks.note: a gang is a pack or band
a lion is an animal

explanation.surface: The headquarters of a pack animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Pack animal suggests a mule or donkey, but the words separate.
explanation.definitionFit: A ganglion is a cluster of nerve cells, literally a centre in the nervous system where nerves meet.

clue.text: Stand and deliver backchat

blocks.note: surface reading: the highwayman's demand to halt and hand over valuables
setter's reading: stand up to someone and give them a cheeky answer back

explanation.surface: A highwayman demands the cheek be handed over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand and deliver' was the highwayman's command; here it means stand firm and send a reply back.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a sharp, witty or angry reply, the kind of quick comeback that counts as cheek.

clue.text: Shopkeeper and medic admitting violation

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the medic surrounds the other word

blocks.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
rape is violation

explanation.surface: A shop owner and a doctor are implicated in an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: D(RAPE)R.
explanation.definitionFit: A draper is a retailer selling cloth and textiles, so a kind of trader with a shop.

clue.text: Get Andersen to order a cab

blocks.note: Hans Christian Andersen, the Danish fairy-tale writer
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: Someone tells the storyteller Andersen to call a taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To order' reads as a verb, but order is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A hansom was a two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage for hire, the Victorian forerunner of the taxi.
